content.text:
Automated validation and rendering were blocked, so I checked the markup by hand instead. Here is where things stand.

**The original file was effectively empty.** It contained only a bare root element with no size, no viewBox, no title, and nothing to draw, so it rendered as a blank default-sized box. The original content, in case you want it back, was:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>
```

**I rewrote it as a complete standalone SVG.** The filename suggested the digit zero, so that is what it now draws. If you intended different artwork, the structure is ready for it and only the path element needs replacing.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="100" height="100" role="img" aria-labelledby="zero-title zero-desc">
  <title id="zero-title">Zero</title>
  <desc id="zero-desc">The digit 0, drawn as an oval ring with slightly heavier sides than top and bottom.</desc>
  <path fill="#1a1a1a" fill-rule="evenodd" d="M50 8 A28 42 0 1 1 50 92 A28 42 0 1 1 50 8 Z M50 18 A16 32 0 1 0 50 82 A16 32 0 1 0 50 18 Z"/>
</svg>
```

What changed:

- **Sizing.** A square viewBox plus explicit width and height give the image an intrinsic size and let it scale cleanly at any resolution.
- **Accessibility.** A title and description, referenced from the root through ARIA attributes, give screen readers something to announce.
- **Content.** The zero is a single path made of an outer oval and an inner oval cut out with the even-odd fill rule. The sides are slightly thicker than the top and bottom, which mimics the stress of a typographic zero. No fonts are involved, so it renders identically everywhere.
- **Standalone header.** An XML declaration with UTF-8 encoding makes the file safe to open directly in editors and viewers.

**What I could not do.** Every command beyond basic directory listing needed approval, and this session has no way to grant it. That blocked the xmllint well-formedness check and a Quick Look render to PNG. I verified the markup by inspection instead: tags are balanced, attributes are quoted, the text contains no characters that need escaping, and both arc pairs span exactly twice their vertical radius, so each forms a closed oval inside the canvas. To confirm visually, open the file in a browser or run this yourself:

```sh
xmllint --noout /private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg
qlmanage -p /private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg
```
